reference_sql:
SELECT promo_id, promo_type,
       COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY promo_type) AS type_promotions
FROM promotions
alternatives:
WITH type_counts AS (  -- one row per promo_type
  SELECT promo_type, COUNT(*) AS n_promos
  FROM promotions
  GROUP BY promo_type
)
SELECT p.promo_id, p.promo_type, tc.n_promos AS type_promotions
FROM promotions p
JOIN type_counts tc ON tc.promo_type = p.promo_type

SELECT p.promo_id, p.promo_type,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM promotions p2 WHERE p2.promo_type = p.promo_type) AS type_promotions
FROM promotions p

other_way.sql:
WITH type_counts AS (  -- one row per promo_type
  SELECT promo_type, COUNT(*) AS n_promos
  FROM promotions
  GROUP BY promo_type
)
SELECT p.promo_id, p.promo_type, tc.n_promos AS type_promotions
FROM promotions p
JOIN type_counts tc ON tc.promo_type = p.promo_type
other_way.tradeoff: Counting per type in a step of its own and joining back is portable, but it reads the table twice.
